01 / THE LADY BEHIND THE ALGORITHM✳

Part countess.
All geek.

Ada Lovelace was an English mathematician and writer. In 1843 she described a method for calculating Bernoulli numbers using Babbage's Analytical Engine. This is why she is often called the first programmer.

In today's terms: she wrote software for a computer that did not yet exist. Courage? Yes. Compatibility? Scheduled for later.

History without our embellishments ↗
1815

Hello, world.

She was born on 10 December in London. Her father was the poet Lord Byron.

Poetry in her DNA. Logic on the roadmap.
1833

Networking with destiny.

She met Charles Babbage and learned about his work on calculating machines.

The best meetup without name badges.
1843

A note that made history.

She added seven extensive notes to her translation of Menabrea's article.

“I only added a few little things.”
∞

A legacy with no expiry date.

She saw the machine's potential beyond ordinary calculation.

We are still battling the printer.

Editor's note: The biographical facts are real. The jokes are ours. Ada did not approve this website - her calendar was already full in 1843.
